cards.text: John, God's servant (Revelation 1:1), has been watching the Lamb, Jesus, God's Son (John 1:29, 34), open the seals on a scroll one by one. Six are already open (Revelation 6). Now the Lamb opens the seventh, the last one, and friend, I'm leaning in SO close.

cards.question: The Lamb opens the seventh seal. What fills heaven?

answers.text: Silence for about half an hour

cards.text: Half an hour of quiet in heaven, and I shared a drawer with dead batteries that argued NONSTOP, so I can't even PICTURE it. Then John sees the seven angels who stand before God.

cards.question: The seven angels who stand before God are given seven ___.

cards.text: Then another angel comes with a golden censer and stands at the golden altar before the throne. He's given much incense to offer.

cards.question: The angel at the golden altar is given much incense to offer. What does he offer along with it?

answers.text: The prayers of all the saints
The crowns of all the elders
The palm branches of the crowd

cards.question: True or false: from the angel's hand, the smoke of the incense and the prayers of the saints fade away before they ever reach God.

cards.text: The prayers of the saints rise up before God, and not ONE of them gets lost in the back of a drawer. Then the angel fills the censer with fire from the altar.

cards.question: The angel's censer is full of fire from the altar. What does he do with it?
True or false: when the angel hurls the censer to the earth, there are peals of thunder, rumblings, flashes of lightning and an earthquake.

cards.text: Now the seven angels with the seven trumpets get ready to sound them. Then the first angel sounds his trumpet.

cards.question: The first angel sounds his trumpet. What is hurled down upon the earth?

answers.text: Hail and fire mixed with blood
Rain and wind mixed with ash
Stones and smoke mixed with dust

cards.question: When the first trumpet sounds, a ___ of the earth is burned up.
True or false: with the first trumpet, a third of the trees are burned up, and all the green grass is burned up too.

cards.text: The second angel sounds his trumpet. Something like a great mountain burning with fire is thrown into the sea, and I'm gripping my gold base with BOTH ends of this mustache.

cards.question: Something like a burning mountain is thrown into the sea. What does a third of the sea turn into?
True or false: with the second trumpet, a third of the ships are destroyed, but every living creature in the sea survives.

cards.text: The third angel sounds his trumpet. A great star burning like a torch falls from heaven onto a third of the rivers and on the springs of water, and that star has a name: Wormwood.

cards.question: The star is named Wormwood. A third of the waters turn ___ like wormwood oil.
True or false: when a third of the waters turn bitter, no one is harmed by them.

cards.text: The fourth angel sounds his trumpet, and a third of the sun and moon and stars are struck. Friend, I light my stars one cookie box at a time, so this one hits me RIGHT in the apron.

cards.question: A third of the sun and moon and stars are struck. What happens?

answers.text: A third of day and night go dark
The sun stands still in the sky
The moon turns red like blood

cards.text: Four trumpets down. Then John hears an eagle flying overhead, calling in a loud voice and crying woe three times on those who dwell on the earth.

cards.question: The eagle cries woe to those who dwell on the earth. What is it warning about?

answers.text: The trumpets of the last three angels
A storm about to hit the seas
A famine coming upon the land

cards.text: When an eagle yells woe three times, friend, I do NOT need to hear it a fourth. Three trumpets still to go, and this story's not done, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: The card says the angel 'stands at the golden altar before the throne.' Revelation 8:3 says he 'came and stood at the altar.' The golden altar before the throne is named only as the place where the incense is offered. The text doesn't say these are the same altar, but the card joins them.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question calls him 'The angel at the golden altar.' This repeats card 5's joining of 'the altar' where he stood (Revelation 8:3) with 'the golden altar before the throne,' which is where the incense is offered.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke 'not ONE of them gets lost in the back of a drawer' puts the saints' prayers inside Papa Dorin's junk drawer. This blends his drawer comparison with the Bible scene of the prayers rising before God.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The blank is the fraction 'third' in 'a ___ of the earth is burned up.' This is the first 'third' in the passage, and nothing before it lets the baker reason it out. It tests exact wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card only restates Revelation 8:3 in plain words, with no reaction, comparison or storyteller line. It has none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card opens the trumpets with two flat sentences restating Revelation 8:6-7. It has no reaction or storyteller line and none of Papa Dorin's voice, even though this is a big turning moment.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
